Extract Motifs from Network Data

Source: R/motifs-extract.R
extract_motifs.Rd

Extracts the triads of a network, classifies each one into the 16 MAN types of a directed network, and optionally tests each triad against a permutation null model. The analysis is individual-level for tna objects and for data with id, and aggregate for matrices, networks and igraph objects.

Usage

extract_motifs(
  x = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  edge_method = c("any", "expected", "percent"),
  edge_threshold = 1.5,
  pattern = c("triangle", "network", "closed", "all"),
  exclude_types = NULL,
  include_types = NULL,
  top = NULL,
  by_type = FALSE,
  min_transitions = 3,
  significance = FALSE,
  n_perm = 100,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Input data. Can be:

  • A tna object (supports individual-level analysis)

  • A matrix (aggregate analysis only, unless data and id provided)

  • A cograph_network object

  • An igraph object

data

Optional data.frame of transitions for individual-level analysis, used together with id. Required columns: from, to and the column(s) named in id. A weight column, or a count column as returned by get_edge_list(), gives the transition weights (1 otherwise). When x is not a tna object, data is used and x is ignored. data without id raises an error of class cograph_data_needs_id.

id

Column name(s) identifying individuals/groups in data. Can be a single string or a character vector; each distinct combination of the values is one individual.

level

Analysis level: "individual" counts how many individuals show each triad, and "aggregate" analyzes the network summed over individuals. The default is "individual" for a tna object or when data and id are supplied, and "aggregate" otherwise. Requesting "individual" without individual data raises a warning and the aggregate level is used.

edge_method

Method for determining edge presence:

"any"

Edge exists if the weight is positive.

"expected"

Edge exists if observed / expected is at least the threshold, with the expectation from the row and column totals.

"percent"

Edge exists if the edge weight divided by the six-edge triad total is at least the threshold.

Default "any".

edge_threshold

Threshold for "expected" or "percent". For "expected", a ratio (1.5 means 50\ values at or below 1 are proportions and values above 1 are percentages, so the default 1.5 means 1.5 percent; set it explicitly for "percent". Ignored when edge_method = "any". Default 1.5.

pattern

Pattern filter for which triads to include:

"triangle"

All 3 node pairs must be connected (any direction). Types: 030C, 030T, 120C, 120D, 120U, 210, 300. Default.

"network"

Excludes the empty triad and the sequential patterns 003, 012 and 021C. Stars and triangles are kept.

"closed"

The 7 closed types, the same set as "triangle".

"all"

All 16 MAN types.

exclude_types

Character vector of MAN types to explicitly exclude. Applied after pattern filter. E.g., c("300") to exclude cliques.

include_types

Character vector of MAN types to include. When supplied, only these types are returned, and pattern and exclude_types are ignored.

top

Number of rows to return, taken after sorting (and after the by_type grouping when by_type = TRUE). NULL or 0 returns all rows. Default NULL.

by_type

If TRUE, the rows are grouped by MAN type in MAN order (003 to 300), keeping the sort order within each type. Default FALSE.

min_transitions

At individual level: minimum total transitions, repeats excluded, for an individual to be analysed. At aggregate level: minimum six-edge weight for a triad to be listed. Default 3, the fewest transitions that can form a closed triad. With probability or relative weights at aggregate level, use 0.

significance

Logical. Run the permutation test? Needs individual-level data. Default FALSE.

n_perm

Number of permutations for the significance test. When significance = TRUE, must be a whole number of at least 2. Default 100.

seed

Optional random seed. The caller's random number state is restored on exit.

Value

A cograph_motif_analysis object, or NULL with a warning when no triad passes the filters. as.data.frame() returns its tables:

what = "results"

One row per node triple and MAN type, with columns triad (display label), node1, node2, node3, type, observed (units showing that type, or the six-edge weight at aggregate level) and, with significance = TRUE, expected, z, p (empirical permutation p-value) and sig (logical, p < 0.05). Rows are sorted by decreasing |z|, or by decreasing observed without significance. A triple that has different types in different individuals appears in more than one row.

what = "types"

One row per MAN type with the total of observed over all rows of that type, before top.

Details

extract_motifs() is subgraphs() with strict = FALSE: a row is one node triple and MAN type, and its observed value is the number of units in which the triple shows that type. Counting, the activity filter and the permutation null are those of subgraphs(), described in motifs(). Self-loops are removed before counting.

Significance needs individual-level data. For aggregate input a warning of class cograph_no_units is raised and the result has no significance columns.

MAN Notation

The 16 triad types use MAN (Mutual-Asymmetric-Null) notation where:

  • First digit: number of mutual (bidirectional) pairs.

  • Second digit: number of asymmetric (one-way) pairs.

  • Third digit: number of null (no edge) pairs.

  • Letter suffix: subtype (C = cycle, T = transitive, D = down, U = up). D and U describe how the type is drawn, not whether it contains an out-star or an in-star.

Pattern Types

The names are those used in the plot titles.

Triangle patterns (all pairs connected):

030C (cycle), 030T (feed-forward), 120C (cycle + mutual), 120D (out-star onto mutual), 120U (in-star from mutual), 210 (near-clique), 300 (clique)

Network patterns:

021D (out-star), 021U (in-star), 102 (mutual pair), 111D (in-star + mutual), 111U (out-star + mutual), 201 (two mutuals), plus all triangle patterns

Sequential patterns (chains):

012 (single edge), 021C (A->B->C chain)

Empty:

003 (no edges)

Printing and plotting

Printing the result shows the analysis settings, the number of units analysed, the MAN type distribution and the first 20 triads. plot() on the result is documented in plot-results.

See also

motifs(), subgraphs(), extract_triads(), motif_census()

Other motifs: extract_triads(), get_edge_list(), motif_census(), motifs(), subgraphs(), triad_census()

Examples

m <- extract_motifs(regulation_net, min_transitions = 0)
m
